text: The Royal Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality (Norwegian: Det kongelige kultur- og likestillingsdepartement; short name Kultur- og likestillingsdepartementet) is responsible for cultural policy, regulations, and matters related to the media and sports, as well as equality and non-discrimination. It was established in 1982 as the Ministry of Cultural and Science, replacing the previous Ministry of Church and Education Affairs, which had held overarching responsibility for cultural affairs until then. The ministry is currently led by Minister of Culture and Equality Lubna Jaffery (Labour), who has held the position since June 2023. The Secretary-General is Kristin Berge, and Aleksander Hagen serves as state secretary, while Mari Hansen Ingleson is the political adviser. The ministry reports to the Storting. The Ministry of Churches and Education, originally founded in 1818, was responsible for culture before the 1982 establishment of the independent Ministry of Culture and Science (Kultur- og vitenskapsdepartementet). In 1990, responsibilities were split into a Ministry of Churches and Culture (Kirke- og kulturdepartementet) and a Ministry of Education and Research (Utdannings- og forskningsdepartementet). In 1991, church responsibilities were transferred back from the Ministry of Culture to the newly renamed Ministry for Churches, Education and Research (Kirke-, utdannings- og forskningsdepartementet). In 2002, the Ministry of Culture regained responsibility for the churches and was renamed Kultur- og kirkedepartementet. From 2010 until the end of 2021, the ministry operated under the name Kulturdepartementet. In 2019, responsibility for equality was transferred from the Ministry of Children and Family to the Ministry of Culture. On 1 January 2022, the ministry was officially renamed Kultur- og likestillingsdepartementet (Ministry of Culture and Equality). The ministry is organized into six departments and an information unit.
